trial_court: Family Court, Shimla, HMA No.157 of 2023
facts_of_case: Marriage solemnized in May 2014; respondent's family harassed petitioner mentally and physically; petitioner left matrimonial home with two minor daughters; respondent's family continued to maltreat her.

legal_principles.principle: While dealing with the issue of transfer of proceedings from one court to another in matrimonial matters, the convenience of wife is to be preferred over convenience of husband.
legal_principles.held: it was held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that in a case where the wife seeks transfer of the petition, then as against husband's convenience, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at.
cited_cases: Sumita Singh v. Kumar Sanjay and another (2001) 10 SCC 41

legal_principles.principle: Once the wife alleges that she has no source of income, whatsoever and was entirely dependent upon his father, then it is the convenience of the wife which was required to be looked into.
legal_principles.held: it was further observed that if the respondent therein had any threat to his life, he could take police help by making an appropriate application to this effect.
cited_cases: Soma Choudhury v. Gourab Choudhaury (2004) 13 SCC 462

legal_principles.principle: The convenience of the wife is the prime consideration in a case seeking transfer of the case at the instance of the wife.
legal_principles.held: it was specifically held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that convenience of wife was the prime consideration.
cited_cases: Rajani Kishor Pardeshi v. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi (2005) 12 SCC 237
use_in: cases seeking transfer of proceedings at the instance of the wife

legal_principles.principle: The Court should consider the balance of convenience or inconvenience to the plaintiff or the defendant or witnesses, and the interest of justice demanding for transfer of suit.
legal_principles.held: it was held: 'balance of convenience or inconvenience to the plaintiff or the defendant or witnesses; convenience or inconvenience of a particular place of trial having regard to the nature of evidence on the points involved in the suit; issues raised by the parties; reasonable apprehension in the mind of the litigant that he might not get justice in the court in which the suit is pending; important questions of law involved or a considerable section of public interested in the litigation; 'interest of justice' demanding for transfer of suit, appeal or other proceeding, etc.
cited_cases: Kulwinder Kaur alias Kulwinder Gurcharan Singh v. Kandi Friends Education Trust and others (2008) 3 SCC 659

outcome.final_order: Petition allowed, seeking transfer of divorce petition from Shimla to Kinnaur.
